AddToCartRequest.description:
POST /v1/cart/items — add or INCREMENT a line.

⚠ The only non-idempotent cart write, because "Add to cart" twice must mean two. `changeId` is therefore REQUIRED: a client-generated UUIDv4 minted once per shopper action and reused by every retry of it, so a request that arrived without its response reaching the client cannot apply twice (FR-018).

ApplyPromoRequest.description: POST /v1/cart/promo — apply a promotional code. Signed-in only (a per-shopper cap needs identity).

BannerDTO.description:
A promotional banner on Home — the shopper-facing face of an advertised promotion (028).

⚠ Every field added in 028 is OPTIONAL, so `customer-web`'s existing consumer keeps typechecking without an edit. What is NOT backward compatible is the LIST: this used to always contain one derived "welcome" stub and is now empty whenever no promotion is advertised. Any layout that assumed at least one banner has to handle `[]`.

code.description: The code a shopper types in the cart. Shown so the banner is actionable, not just decorative.

href.description: Retained for `customer-web`. Mobile ignores it in favour of `target`.

key.description: The promotion id. Stable across reads — clients use it as a list key.

placement.description:
Which of Home's two placements this banner occupies (029 FR-027). **Exclusive** — never both.

⚠ Optional, and absent means `"carousel"` — matching the column default, so a client reading a server that has not been redeployed degrades to the safe case rather than losing the banner.

position.description:
Where this banner sits in Home's section sequence: 0 above the first section, n after the nth.

⚠ `WireInt`, NOT `number`. 027 lost days to Kotlin serialising a quantity as `Double`, the wire carrying `1.0`, and Go's `encoding/json` refusing `1.0` into an `int` — while every unit test passed, because the fakes spoke Kotlin at both ends and never crossed the wire. The fix was made at the contract so the generated Kotlin cannot regress; this field takes the same treatment.

terms.description:
The condition sentence, e.g. `"On orders over $30"` — COMPOSED SERVER-SIDE from the promotion's minimum, so both surfaces phrase one promotion identically. Null when it has no conditions.

FR-037d: a shopper must learn of a condition from the banner or from where it leads — never first at payment.

BannerPlacement.description:
Where an advertised promotion appears on Home (029 FR-027). **Exclusive** — never both.

⚠ Declared ONCE, here, and imported by both `storefront.ts` (the shopper-facing banner) and `promotion.ts` (the operator-facing promotion). It was briefly declared in both, which typechecked in each file alone and collided the moment the package re-exported them — the same union in two places is precisely the drift Principle II exists to prevent.

BannerTarget.description:
Where a promotional banner leads (028).

⚠ A CLOSED vocabulary, deliberately. `href` below is a WEB PATH, and mobile has no URL router — inventing one to serve a banner would be the tail wagging the dog. A closed set the server promises and each client maps exhaustively means a new target shows up as a gap in a `when`/`switch` at compile time, and at runtime an unrecognised value renders the banner NON-TAPPABLE. A tap that does nothing is worse than no tap.

⚠ `promotion` was ADDED after every banner shipped targeting `search`, which sent every tap to the unfiltered store — the Search tab by another name, carrying none of the promotion's facts. FR-034 (no banner-only destinations) was read as forbidding a promotion screen; it does not. That rule protects shoppers from CONTENT reachable only via a carousel slide, and a promotion detail contains nothing the banner face does not already announce — it is the banner's own message, stated in full. See `PromotionDTO`.

CartBlockedReason.description: Why checkout is unavailable, when it is.

CartCheckoutStateDTO.description: Whether the shopper may proceed, and if not, why — so the cart can say it up front instead of letting them walk into a refusal at payment (FR-054). Also enforced server-side at intent (FR-056).

minimumSubtotalAmount.description: Null when no minimum is in force; then nothing is shown at all (FR-057).

remainingAmount.description: How much more is needed to reach the minimum. Null unless `blockedReason` is "below_minimum".

CartDTO.description: The full cart — returned by GET /v1/cart AND by every mutating response, so a client never has to guess the outcome of a change or issue a follow-up read (FR-007).

deliveryFeeAmount.description: Always "0.00" here: delivery is priced at the delivery step, once a destination exists (FR-063).

itemSubtotalAmount.description: Payable, available lines only — unavailable items are never charged for (FR-022).

revision.description: Monotonic, bumped by every mutation. The client mirror adopts a response only when this exceeds what it holds, which is how an out-of-order reply cannot overwrite a newer cart (FR-009).

savedLines.description: Set aside for later: kept, shown honestly, and counted in NO total (FR-028…FR-031).

CartDiscountDTO.description: The discount currently applying, recomputed on every read — never a stored or client-sent amount.

amount.description: The computed reduction, capped so the payable total can never fall below zero.

label.description: e.g. "20% off" — display only, and shop-free.

CartDiscountKind.description: What a discount takes off. A NAMED type on purpose: an inline `"percentage" | "fixed"` union makes the Kotlin generator emit a class called `Kind`, which is the same generic-name trap that produced 019's bare `Line` class. Named here, it generates `CartDiscountKind`.

CartLimitsDTO.description: The platform's ceilings, sent so the client can explain them rather than guess them (FR-037/038).

CartLineDTO.description: A cart line, or a set-aside line — the same shape; re-priced against the catalog on every read.

packageKey.description: OPAQUE package grouping key (021). Items sharing a packageKey ship together as one anonymous "package" (one per fulfilling shop). It is NOT a shop id, name, or location — a meaningless-to-the- customer token that lets the cart show the split (021 FR-005a) while revealing no shop (SC-006).

priceChangedFrom.description: The price this line was added at, when it differs from `unitPriceAmount` — so the shopper is told what it *was* rather than being surprised at payment (FR-023). Null when unchanged, and null for a line added before the platform recorded add-time prices (a pre-migration row must not fabricate a change). The shopper always pays `unitPriceAmount`, in both directions.

CartLineInput.description: One line of a client-supplied set (merge, preview).

detail.description: Human-readable specifics where the kind alone is not enough. NEVER names or implies a shop.

CartNoticeKind.description: A notice the cart surfaces before checkout. `productId` is null for a cart-level notice (a promotional code that stopped applying) — a widening of 019's shape, inert for existing readers, which match on `kind` and `productId` together.

CartPolicyDTO.description: GET /v1/cart/policy — PUBLIC. The minimum and the ceilings, so a guest cart can gate and explain honestly without a server cart to read them from.

CartPreviewRequest.description: POST /v1/cart/preview — PUBLIC. Re-price a guest's device cart with full notices and write nothing, so a restored guest cart shows current prices and availability too (FR-004 applies to guests).

CheckoutDeliveryMethod.description: The three delivery service levels (021). Availability per package follows from the shop's origin zone and the customer's destination zone — never from shop identity, which the customer never sees.

ConfirmCheckoutRequest.description: POST /v1/checkout/confirm — fallback finalizer (covers a delayed/missed webhook).

CreateAddressRequest.description: POST /v1/addresses — the first address created becomes the default.

CreateCheckoutIntentRequest.description: POST /v1/checkout/intent — create/locate the pending order and its PaymentIntent (019, extended 021).

addressId.description: The SHIPPING address (required). Serviceability + delivery pricing key off this (021).

billingAddressId.description: 023: the BILLING address, when the customer diverged from shipping. Absent / null / equal to `addressId` → billing is "same as shipping" (the order stores NULL). Billing never affects the amount or the quote.

excludedPackageKeys.description: 021: packages the customer confirmed proceeding WITHOUT (auto-set-aside undeliverable items). MUST exactly match the server's unserviceable set or the intent is refused (FR-006b, SC-011a).

quoteId.description: 021: the captured quote being placed. Honored while unexpired; else 409 → re-quote.

selections.description: 021: the customer's per-package method choices (default preference + overrides, resolved).

clientSecret.description: Authorizes confirming exactly this PaymentIntent from the client. Never a secret key.

deliveryBreakdown.description: 021: the per-package delivery breakdown, for the order summary. Anonymous.

DeliveryBreakdownLineDTO.description: One line of the per-package delivery breakdown on the intent response (021). Anonymous.

DeliveryMethodOptionDTO.description: One selectable delivery option for a package (021). Server-computed; the client never sends a fee.

scheduleDates.description: Selectable dates for method='scheduled'; null otherwise.

window.description: Derived window, e.g. "Today by 6pm" / "in 2–3 days"; null for a scheduled method (pick a date).

DeliveryQuoteRequest.description: POST /v1/checkout/quote — per-package delivery options for the cart + address (021 US1).

expiresAt.description: The captured quote is honored until this instant; after it the customer must re-quote (021 R7).

DeliverySelectionDTO.description: The customer's chosen method for one package (021). Carries NO fee — the server prices it (SC-004).

FavoriteDTO.description: A saved product (product card fields + when it was saved).

MediaDTO.description: A product image (presigned GET URL + alt text).

MergeCartRequest.description:
POST /v1/cart/merge — fold a device cart into the account cart at sign-in.

⚠ UNION WITH MAXIMUM QUANTITY per product. This is NOT 019's original `/v1/cart/merge`, which SUMMED quantities and was removed on 2026-07-23 after it tripled carts. Taking the maximum makes the operation idempotent AND commutative: signing in twice, or retrying an interrupted merge, leaves exactly the same cart (FR-011, FR-012). Nothing from either side is dropped.

OrderAddressDTO.description: The snapshotted delivery address on the receipt.

billingAddress.description: The BILLING address snapshot (023). `null` means "same as shipping" — the client renders "Billing: same as shipping" rather than repeating the address. A value is a divergent billing address. NEVER exposed to the shop (FR-018). Absent/null on pre-023 orders.

deliveryAddress.description: The SHIPPING address snapshot (the main one — where the order is delivered).

discountAmount.description: The promotional discount applied at payment (027 FR-049). The platform's own computation at that moment, stored on the order — so a receipt stays explainable years later even if the code has since been changed or disabled. "0.00" (or absent, on a pre-027 order) when no code was used. Invariant: grandTotal = itemSubtotal + deliveryFee − discount.

promoCode.description: The literal code used, denormalised beside the discount so the receipt can still say "SPRING20" independently of the promotion record. Null/absent when no code was used.

OrderFulfillmentDTO.description:
An anonymous per-shop fulfillment portion — NO shop identity (FR-033).

020 gave `status` a life: 019 created every portion `pending` and no code path ever changed it. The values now span the shop's real working lifecycle. Still no shop name, id, or count that would imply WHO is fulfilling (FR-018, SC-009).

deliveryServiceLevel.description: The delivery this portion was bought with (021) — still ANONYMOUS (no shop). The customer's receipt breakdown shows, per package, what they paid to have it delivered and when it is promised. Absent on pre-021 orders.

unavailableItems.description: Present ONLY when the portion has reached a terminal state (FR-018b). Absent while picking.

OrderItemDTO.description: A line on the receipt (product snapshot — never a shop).

OrderShortfallDTO.description:
An item the customer paid for and will NOT receive (020 FR-018b).

Disclosed at item level, but ONLY once the portion is terminal — a flag raised and then undone mid-pick must never reach the customer (SC-017). Naming the customer's own item discloses nothing about fulfillment structure (FR-018c).

Carries NO refund promise: no money moves in 020, and the shortfall is left deliberately visible for a later refunds slice to resolve (FR-010b, FR-018a).

OrderStatus.description: Order lifecycle mirrored to the client (payment-driven).

OrderSummaryDTO.description: A row in the order history (GET /v1/orders).

promoCode.description: 027 — set when a promotional code was used, so history can mark a discounted order.

PaymentStatus.description: Payment outcome mirrored from the Stripe PaymentIntent.

ProductAttributeGroupDTO.description: A labelled group of attribute rows on the product detail page (never laid out as cards).

ProductBadge.description: A badge shown on a product card. Derived server-side (on_sale = has compare-at; new = newest).

ProductSearchResultDTO.description:
A page of search results with a keyset cursor for infinite scroll.

⚠ `cursor` is OPAQUE and sort-tagged. Do not construct one, and do not carry one across a sort change — the server rejects a cursor issued under a different ordering with 400 `cursor_sort_mismatch`, because honouring it would silently drop and repeat products (FR-016b).

sort.description: The ordering ACTUALLY applied — may differ from the request. Render the sort control from this, not from what was asked for, or the control will misdescribe the list beneath it.

total.description: Total products matching the refinements, ignoring pagination (025 FR-016a).

ProductSort.description:
The orderings a result set can be presented in (025 FR-016).

`relevance` is only meaningful alongside a text query; without one the server falls back to `newest` and reports what it actually did in `ProductSearchResultDTO.sort`.

PromotionDTO.description:
One advertised promotion in full — the destination of a banner tap (`GET /v1/storefront/promotions/:id`).

⚠ WHY A PROMOTION HAS NO OTHER DESTINATION. `promo_code` carries no product or category scoping: a promotion is a whole-cart discount with an optional minimum. There is no set of qualifying products to filter a results list to, so a banner pointed at one was always pointing at nothing in particular. A cart-level code is a message, and the destination for a message is the message itself.

⚠ Served through the SAME visibility predicate Home used, so a promotion that expired, was exhausted or was withdrawn between Home loading and the tap is **404, not stale terms** (028 FR-036). This is also why the response is uncached.

code.description: NON-nullable, unlike `BannerDTO.code` — a screen whose purpose is to hand over a code must have one.

terms.description: The same sentence `BannerDTO.terms` carries, from the same server-side composer.

validity.description:
How long is left — `"Ends in 3 days"`, `"Ends tomorrow"`. Null when the promotion never ends.

⚠ RELATIVE, not a calendar date, and composed server-side. A date means nothing without a timezone and the platform has no timezone concept; a duration reads the same from anywhere. Mobile additionally has no date formatting of any kind, so a raw timestamp could not be rendered there.

serviceable.description: False when this package cannot be delivered to the address (021 US2). methods is then empty.

QuotePackageItemDTO.description: One ANONYMOUS package in a quote (021) — the items from a single shop, shown without any shop identity or location (FR-019). `packageKey` is an opaque grouping token.

ReorderRequest.description: POST /v1/cart/reorder — put a past order's items back in the cart (FR-034). Union-with-maximum against the current cart, so a double tap cannot double quantities.

ReorderResultDTO.description: The reorder outcome: the resulting cart plus exactly what could not come back, so the shopper is told rather than left to notice (FR-035). The report names no shop.

ReorderSkipReason.description: Why an item from a past order could not be added back.

ServiceabilityDTO.description:
Whether Effy delivers to a location, answered BEFORE a cart exists (025 FR-014).

⚠ Deliberately just the answer. No delivery fee or window (FR-014a — both depend on cart contents, so anything shown here is an estimate checkout would revise), and no zone id or name (FR-006 — zone names are geographic and would disclose where Effy fulfils from).

postcode.description: The normalised postcode the answer applies to.

StorefrontCategoryDTO.description: A browse/filter category, customer projection (GET /v1/storefront/categories). Distinct from the admin/shop `CategoryDTO` in catalog.ts — this carries no internal id/status/order.

imageUrl.description: Representative image, DERIVED from a product in the category — categories store no imagery, and 025 FR-001 forbids adding a column for it. Null → the client renders a brand tile, never a broken frame. The choice is deterministic so a category does not change its face between page loads.

productCount.description: Active products in this category (025). Drives "N items" and the empty-category case.

StorefrontProductCardDTO.description: The at-a-glance product card used in rails, search results, favorites and recently-viewed.

StorefrontProductDetailDTO.description: Full product detail (gallery, description, grouped attributes, category path).

categoryKey.description: The primary category's key — drives the related-products rail (025 FR-026). `categoryPath` carries display NAMES, which cannot be used to query.

StorefrontRailDTO.description: A merchandising rail on Home (Featured / On-sale / a category rail).

UpdateCartLineRequest.description:
PATCH /v1/cart/items/{productId} — set an ABSOLUTE line quantity; 0 removes.

Absolute, not a delta, which is what lets the client debounce ten taps into one request and drop the intermediate values safely (FR-016). Idempotent, so `changeId` is optional; clients send it anyway so the queue has no special cases.

WireInt.description:
A whole number on the wire.

⚠ THIS ALIAS IS LOAD-BEARING, and it exists because a plain `number` broke every mobile cart write.

TypeScript `number` becomes JSON Schema `"number"`, which the Kotlin generator renders as `Double` — so `kotlinx.serialization` sent `"quantity":1.0`, and Go's `encoding/json` **cannot** unmarshal `1.0` into an `int`. Every `POST /v1/cart/items` and `PATCH /v1/cart/items/{id}` from customer-mobile therefore failed to bind and answered 422. `customer-web` was unaffected: JavaScript serialises an integer as `1`, with no decimal point.

`@asType integer` makes the schema say `"integer"`, which generates a Kotlin `Long` and puts a whole number on the wire. Use it for EVERY count, quantity, limit and revision in this contract — the response direction was always fine (kotlinx accepts `3` for a Double), so the asymmetry hid it.

See specs/027-customer-cart-sync/research.md R13.

description: Aggregator — codegen entry only (see file header). Every field forces a type into the schema.
